subject: Audit data transfer, redaction options, and export playbook
messages:
From: Sarah Dunn <sarah@atlasfinancial.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit log export requirements and delivery options

Jonas,

Thanks for taking our RFP. A few follow-ups from the security and compliance side so we can evaluate Redwood for a potential production deployment: we need a written description of how we could obtain bulk audit data (authentication/authorization trails, API call logs, user-level event history) on demand. Please include:

- Export formats you support (NDJSON, CSV, Parquet, other).
- Redaction options for PII before export (automatic field masking, tokenization, redaction rules and their scope).
- Chain-of-custody/manifest that accompanies a bulk export (checksums, record counts, timestamps).
- Encryption in transit and at rest for exported bundles.
- Typical SLA/turnaround for an on-demand bulk extract and for regular scheduled snapshots.
- Delivery methods (S3 PUT with presigned URLs, secure FTP, encrypted transfer to customer-managed bucket, FedRamp-compatible options if available).

Also: do you provide an attestable tamper-evidence mechanism (e.g., signed manifests or digest logs) and do you support scoped exports for a subset of users/teams for legal holds?

If you can attach a short playbook or a one-page matrix mapping export options to evidence delivered, that would be ideal. Can we aim to have this by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Dunn
Head of Security Programs
Atlas Financial

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Dunn <sarah@atlasfinancial.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log export requirements and delivery options

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. I've attached a short playbook (Redwood_Audit_Export_Playbook_v1.pdf) that maps export types to the artifacts we provide. High-level answers below, and I can schedule a 30-min runthrough if helpful.

- Formats: NDJSON and Parquet are our primary supported bulk formats. We also offer CSV for simple slices (note: CSV can lose schema fidelity).
- Redaction: We support pre-export redaction pipelines (rule-based redaction and field-level tokenization). Redaction rules are defined at export time and can be scoped by project, team, or user id. For sensitive PII we offer deterministic tokenization so referential integrity is preserved without exposing raw values.
- Manifest & chain-of-custody: Every export bundle includes a machine-readable manifest with record counts, per-file SHA256 checksums, start/end timestamps, export job id, and a signed digest (we sign manifests with our platform key; for higher-assurance workflows we can include an HSM-backed signature option).
- Encryption: All transfer options are TLS 1.3 by default. At-rest encryption on export bundles is AES-256. For customer-managed buckets we support server-side encryption using customer KMS keys and pre-signed, KMS-encrypted uploads.
- SLAs / turnaround: On-demand extracts for bounded slices (<= 250GB) are typically delivered within 24–48 hours. Bulk archive exports (multi-TB) follow a scoped project timeline — typical delivery within 5 business days depending on size and retention tier. We include estimated transfer time in the export job summary.
- Delivery methods: S3 PUT to customer-managed buckets (recommended), presigned S3 URLs, or secure transfer to an SFTP endpoint. We can also stage encrypted bundles in a temporary, access-restricted bucket and hand off keys via your KMS.

We can generate scoped exports for legal-hold cases and include a preservation flag that prevents deletion until release.

I'm looping in Priyom (exports lead) and Laura (compliance) — Priyom can share the manifest schema and sample outputs.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
A: +1 415 555 0192

Attachment: Redwood_Audit_Export_Playbook_v1.pdf (3 pages)

From: Sarah Dunn <sarah@atlasfinancial.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasfinancial.com>, security@atlasfinancial.com
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log export requirements and delivery options

Thanks Jonas — that addresses a lot. A couple of clarifying items from our legal/forensics team: 

1) For manifests: do you include a per-record identifier that we can use to reconcile against our own event store (e.g., stable event_id across exports)? We want to be able to verify that a slice returned from Redwood exactly matches the subset of events we requested.

2) For redaction: is there an audit trail that shows what redaction rule was applied to each exported record (so investigators can see if a rule masked a value)?

3) Chain-of-custody: can you provide example tooling or checksum verification commands we would run on receipt? And, for very large exports, do you provide multipart manifesting so we can verify individual parts as they arrive?

If you can include a sample manifest and a tiny sample export (pseudonymized) we can run an internal reconciliation test. We're fine with S3 delivery into a customer-managed bucket; please provide the manifest schema and a sample CSV/NDJSON that aligns.

-Sarah

From: priyom_das@redwood.com <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Dunn <sarah@atlasfinancial.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log export requirements and delivery options

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — attaching a small set of artifacts to accelerate your reconciliation test:

- audit_export_manifest_schema.jsonl (attachment) — this is the manifest schema we emit. Key fields: export_job_id, sequence_range (start_ts/end_ts), file_list, record_count, sha256_checksum, signature, redaction_profile, dataset_scope.
- sample_delivery_manifest.csv (attachment) — a tiny sample (10 rows) showing per-file checksums and record counts.
- sample_pseudonymized_slice.ndjson (hosted link in playbook) — a redacted, representative slice you can use for verification.

Direct answers to your questions:

1) Per-record identifiers: exports preserve an internal stable event_id. That id is included in exports unless customers request removal as part of a PII purge. For pseudonymization/tokenization we provide a deterministic token that maps consistently across exports when the same tokenization key is used.

2) Redaction audit trail: the manifest includes a redaction_profile field and for exports where record-level masking occurs we also emit a redaction_map file that lists records subject to redaction and the rule id applied. That map is hash-referenced in the manifest so you can verify integrity without exposing raw values.

3) Chain-of-custody verification: We publish the manifest with per-file SHA256 checksums. For multipart transfers we include part-level checksums and an overall bundle checksum. Verification commands we recommend are shown in the attachment (simple sh + openssl/sha256sum examples). For HSM-backed signing workflows we can provide the public verification key and a verification script.

Next steps: I can provision a short-lived test bucket and push the sample slice if you want to run reconciliation. If the test looks good we can formalize the export SLA in the SOW and add the HSM signing option as part of the compliance addendum.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Engineering Manager, Data Exports | Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit_export_manifest_schema.jsonl, sample_delivery_manifest.csv
